channel.title: Yaprflow Updates
channel.description: Signed updates for Yaprflow for Mac.

item.description:
# Yaprflow 5.2.16
- Shrinks the live Quick Dictation audio-level overlay to 208 × 36 points, with a shorter waveform and tight spacing around the recording indicator. - Preparation and error messages resize only when they need more room. - Includes the transcription boundary improvements from 5.2.14 and the menu bar status colors from 5.2.15.
Speech recognition remains on the Mac.

# Yaprflow 5.2.13
This release improves recording feedback and permission recovery:
- Quick Dictation now shows a live microphone-level waveform while recording instead of displaying partial transcription text. - Dictation continues to transcribe natural, bounded sections with Parakeet, keeping long recordings memory-safe while preserving final accuracy. - Meeting Notes now lets ScreenCaptureKit verify Screen & System Audio access directly after a Sparkle update instead of stopping on a stale preliminary permission result. - If macOS genuinely denies capture, Yaprflow still provides a direct route to the correct Privacy & Security settings.
All speech recognition remains on the Mac. Audio is not uploaded for transcription.

# Yaprflow 5.2.12
This release upgrades on-device Mac transcription and adds natural spoken punctuation:
- Quick Dictation and Meeting Notes now use NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 for substantially faster, highly accurate offline transcription. - Parakeet automatically detects 25 supported European languages without a manual language setting. - Dictation is finalized at natural pauses, while long meetings are processed in bounded sections so one- and two-hour sessions do not accumulate audio in memory. - Meeting Notes continue to separate microphone speech from Mac system audio and remove system-audio echo from the “Me” transcript. - In Polished mode, spoken commands such as “period,” “question mark,” “comma,” “new line,” and “new paragraph” produce natural formatting. - Exact dictation mode continues to preserve recognized words verbatim.
All speech recognition remains on the Mac. Audio is not uploaded for transcription.
